title: Amritsar's Singh Sabha, 1873
hookLine: Sikhs in Amritsar formed a society to renew teaching, schools and literature

cards: A room in Amritsar. A group of Sikh gentlemen sit together, worried. The kingdom is gone.
The old schools are thin. Printed books in Punjabi are hard to find. And news has come that some Sikh students at a mission school plan to leave the faith.
Nobody in the room has an army. What they have is a meeting, and by the end of it, they've founded a society with a plain name.

teach.h: SINGH SABHA — SOCIETY OF THE SINGHS.
teach.b: First, the name. Singh, the lion, is the name Khalsa men take. Sabha means an assembly or society.
So Singh Sabha is simply the society of the Singhs, a gathering of Sikhs with a purpose. Second, the worry.
After the loss of the kingdom, Sikh leaders saw learning slipping away. Histories say the spark included word that a few Sikh students at a Christian mission school were about to be baptized.

Missionaries were active in the Punjab and debated in the open. The founders' answer, as the histories tell it, was to turn inward: to teach their own young people their own Gurus. Third, what they set out to do.
Renew Sikh teaching as the Gurus gave it. Open schools.
Print books and papers in Punjabi, in the Gurmukhi letters. Welcome back those who had drifted away. And, under British rule, seek the goodwill of officials for their schools.

teach.h: WHERE THE ONE NAME IS SPOKEN.
teach.b: In a hymn in Sri Rag, Guru Nanak asks how the true congregation is recognized, and answers: it's where the One Name is spoken.
The Singh Sabha was a congregation for a new age, not a court or a camp, but people sitting together to study and teach.
In the years that followed, other Singh Sabhas sprang up in other towns, and tomorrow you'll meet a bolder one.
Renewal, here, begins in a room with a few chairs.

how: Sikhs remember the Singh Sabha of Amritsar as the start of a renewal of Sikh teaching, schools and Punjabi books; study circles and gurdwara classes carry on that work today.

games.q: you're in Amritsar. the kingdom is gone and learning is slipping. what do you do first?
o: found a society to open schools and print books.

practice: Think of two or three people who might like to learn something with you, a text, a skill, a question you share, and picture the place: a kitchen table, a call, a corner of a library.
See the first ten minutes: one reads, the others listen, someone asks a question. If you pray, ask in your own words for a good sangat, the company of seekers.
